speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources how have the recent fires in Australia affected Singapore’s environment and food security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This level of air quality is comparable to the same period in previous years.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Australia is an important source of commonly consumed food items for Singapore, such as meat, milk and sugar.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, we hope that it does not happen in Australia, the bushfires, but if it continues to occur in future, is it conceivable that this could come to Singapore	– meaning that the winds change direction	– and is it conceivable for fires in Australia to reach Singapore, and in such an instance, what preparations do we need to make?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Again, I hear our vision of "30 by 30".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We know where the fires, when they burn, affect us almost annually.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, thankfully, I do not think we have to worry yet unless something in the weather patterns change or the intensity of the fire goes beyond this year and last year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Because when we have a situation 20, 30, 40 years down the line, when everywhere in the world, food growing will be a challenge, we probably have to be prepared to know how to grow food now, to grow in ways that we do not normally or conventionally do.
